title: Comparing NCM And CDM
definition: The Non-Cooperation Movement (NCM, 1920-22) and Civil Disobedience Movement (CDM, 1930-34) represent the two major mass-mobilization phases of the Indian National Movement under Gandhi, transitioning from 'non-cooperation' with colonial institutions to 'active defiance' of colonial laws.
importanceInUpsc: UPSC frequently tests the evolution of Gandhian strategy, the shift in social base, and the ideological transition from 'Swaraj' (self-rule) to 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Comparing NCM And CDM.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, Khilafat Issue, Simon Commission, Nehru Report
